headline: Highest risk is data leakage: social-auto-upload has broad network egress while dagster is a local orchestrator, creating a plausible path for sensitive pipeline outputs to leave the workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, and dagster cannot read files or use MCP. However, social-auto-upload exposes file inputs and CLI-based tool use, so manual copy-paste or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content influence downstream steps. The pairwise pathway is weak and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies dagster-generated text into social-auto-upload inputs
IF a shared folder is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text between tools
Use a human review step before any upload command
Rename or segregate input files by source
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to handoff files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no network egress, but social-auto-upload has broad network egress and handles account data plus media files. If dagster outputs sensitive pipeline artifacts into files that social-auto-upload consumes, those contents can be transmitted to third parties during upload. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, though not proven here.
conditions: IF dagster writes sensitive artifacts into files later selected by social-auto-upload
IF social-auto-upload uploads a file containing confidential content
mitigations: Restrict upload directories to non-sensitive media only
Review file names before each upload run
Use a staging folder with redacted copies
Disable uploads from shared pipeline outputs
requires-engineering: enforce content classification before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot directly contend for mutable resources with social-auto-upload. Social-auto-upload supports multiple instances and uses one account file per account name, which reduces but does not eliminate coordination issues if operators reuse the same account file manually. The overlap is limited and mostly operational.
conditions: IF two social-auto-upload instances target the same account file
IF an operator manually edits shared account files while dagster jobs run
mitigations: Assign one account file per instance
Avoid concurrent edits to account files
Serialize upload jobs per account
Keep dagster outputs read-only to the uploader
requires-engineering: add file locking around account files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can produce pipeline outputs, and social-auto-upload can act on files and send them to external platforms. If social-auto-upload treats dagster-produced artifacts as ready-to-publish without verification, a bad upstream artifact can cascade into an incorrect or public upload. The pairwise risk exists in default workflows where outputs are handed off directly.
conditions: IF dagster output is used as the upload payload without a review step
IF social-auto-upload publishes files generated by dagster
mitigations: Insert a manual approval step before upload
Validate file type and destination before publishing
Use a checksum or manifest for approved assets
Separate generation and publication directories
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Social-auto-upload touches account data and media and can transmit them to external platforms, while dagster is a data orchestrator with no declared data classes. If EU personal data or regulated media is routed through social-auto-upload without a matching DPA or residency control, compliance gaps can arise. Dagster is not the compliance bottleneck; the uploader is.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is included in uploaded media or metadata
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or residency review for the target platform
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from uploads
Review retention settings on the target platform
Document the lawful basis for each upload workflow
Limit account access to approved operators
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy checks
